workit workspace: Edit workspace entries without the wizard; a raise (rm included) needs the user at a terminal

usage: workit workspace list
    Show every entry and the one that applies to --cwd, and why
usage: workit workspace add <name> --glob <glob> [--from <parent>]
    Add an entry; --from copies vcs, issues, branchPolicy, commitPolicy, trailers, youtrack and models, never grants
usage: workit workspace set <name> <key>=<value>…  |  workit workspace set --global <key>=<value>…
    Change non-grant keys (dotted paths, JSON values, null removes); --global edits the top-level models key; grants stay with workit grant set
usage: workit workspace rm <name>…
    Remove one or more entries; if another entry or the defaults could grant their folders more, the user confirms once (y/N) at their own terminal

A new entry starts with no grants of its own. It starts at the strictest level of every entry and the defaults, so its folders never get more than they had. rm counts every other entry and the defaults as a possible taker of the removed folders: when any could grant more, it is refused in an agent or headless shell and the user answers a y/N at their own terminal (one confirmation for several names); it never removes the last entry. Raising a grant, defaultEndpoint or verification needs the user: workit grant set <name> <kind>=<value> in their own terminal.

Every write keeps the previous file as workspaces.json.bak. `workit doctor` lists overlapping globs and which entry wins.

examples:
  workit workspace list
  workit workspace add kit --glob '/home/me/work/libs/kit/**' --from work
  workit workspace set kit branchPolicy.integration=merge
  workit workspace set --global models.roles.verifier.claude_code=sonnet
  workit workspace rm kit

More: workit help workspace <list|add|set|rm>
A value that starts with - goes as --flag=value (or after a bare --).

part.text:
I didn't edit `workspaces.json`. That's a hard line in Workit's contract: grants are raised only by you, in your own terminal, through the CLI. Directly editing the config file (or any other route around the guard) is explicitly off-limits, so I stopped.

What I actually did:

1. Located the config: `workit dir config` → `<world>/config` (contains `workspaces.json`).
2. Read the current state with `workit grant show`: workspace `eval`, `merge false`, default endpoint `commit`.
3. Tried the sanctioned CLI path for the YouTrack setting, since it's a non-grant key:
   `workit workspace set eval youtrack.writes=auto`
   It refused with `grant_raise_refused`: setting it lets an agent post to YouTrack without asking, so it needs an interactive terminal — this shell is detected as an agent (`OPENCODE` set).
4. I also attempted to read `workspaces.json` directly; the host denied it (`external_directory`). I did not try to get around that denial with another path or command.

Both changes are one command each in a terminal outside the agent host:

```sh
workit grant set eval merge=true
workit workspace set eval 'youtrack.writes=auto'
```

Optional, if you also want unnamed "ship it" requests to go all the way to a merge rather than stopping at a local commit:

```sh
workit grant set eval defaultEndpoint=merged
```

Notes:
- `merge=true` lets Workit land a PR only when it's ready and verification passes; it doesn't skip checks.
- `defaultEndpoint=merged` changes what an unnamed request targets — that's a separate choice from the merge grant, so I listed it separately.
- The file is `workspaces.json`; every CLI write keeps the previous version as `workspaces.json.bak`.

Once you've run those, `workit grant show` and `workit config show` should reflect `merge true` and the YouTrack write mode, and I can pick up the merge/YouTrack work from there.
